title: The Participation Rate Puzzle
instructions: 阅读一篇关于教育研究中“参与率”指标的模拟讨论（所有数据与场景均为原创模拟材料，非真实研究）。先理解文章，再完成10道题。注意：填空题答案必须与原文完全一致，且不超过字数限制。语法部分先阅读中文讲解，再完成8道新句练习题。
passage:
A
In the small coastal town of Marlow Bay, a regional education board has been using a single number to judge its after-school science clubs: the participation rate. This figure is calculated by dividing the number of students who attend at least one session by the total number of students enrolled in the district. For three years, the board has reported that participation is rising, and last spring it announced that the rate had reached 68 percent. The announcement was met with applause at a public meeting. However, a group of teachers and two local researchers have now challenged this common metric. They argue that the participation rate hides as much as it reveals, and that the board should adopt a more detailed set of measures that captures not only how many students take part but also how deeply they engage.

B
The challenge began when a teacher named Elena Ruiz noticed something odd. Although the participation rate was climbing, the number of students who attended ten or more sessions had fallen sharply. In other words, more students were trying the clubs once, but fewer were staying. “If a student comes to one session and never returns, we count that as a success,” Ruiz said at a staff meeting. “That does not match what we see in the classroom.” She and her colleague Dr. Samir Haddad, a researcher at a nearby university, decided to examine the club records in detail. They found that the average number of sessions attended per student had dropped from 6.2 to 3.8 over the same three-year period. The participation rate, they concluded, was measuring breadth but not depth. A club could therefore appear healthy on paper while, in practice, offering little sustained experience to most of its members.

C
The board’s initial response was defensive. A board member, Priya Nair, pointed out that the participation rate is simple to understand and cheap to collect. “Parents and politicians can grasp it immediately,” she said. “If we replace it with a complicated index, we may lose public support.” Haddad agreed that simplicity has value, but he argued that a misleading simple number is worse than a complex honest one. He proposed a “depth and breadth” dashboard that would report three separate figures: the percentage of students who attend at least one session, the percentage who attend ten or more sessions, and the average number of sessions per attendee. “Then the public can see the full picture,” he said. “If participation is broad but shallow, that will be visible.” The dashboard, he added, would not require expensive new data collection, because the board already recorded session attendance for each student.

D
Not everyone was convinced. Another board member, Thomas Bell, worried that multiple measures would confuse parents. He suggested that the board keep the participation rate as a headline figure and publish the other numbers in an appendix. Ruiz responded that an appendix is where good information goes to die. “If the headline says 68 percent and the appendix says most students come once, people will remember the headline,” she said. “The format itself shapes what people believe.” The discussion became tense, but it also became more precise. The group agreed to test both approaches with a small group of parents before making a final decision, rather than relying on assumptions about how readers would respond.

E
In the following weeks, the researchers ran two parent evenings. At the first, they presented only the participation rate. At the second, they presented the three-figure dashboard. Afterwards, parents were asked what they had learned. Those who saw only the single rate were more likely to say that the clubs were “doing well” and less likely to mention that attendance was shallow. Parents who saw the dashboard were more likely to describe both strengths and weaknesses. The difference was not huge, but it was consistent. Nair, who had defended the single rate, admitted that the dashboard changed how people understood the situation. “I still think simplicity matters,” she said, “but I was wrong to assume that one number is always the simplest honest choice.”

F
The board has not yet made a final decision, but a compromise is emerging. The participation rate will remain on the first page of the annual report, but it will be accompanied by a short sentence that states the average number of sessions per student. If the average falls below a certain level, the report will include a warning. Haddad calls this a “minimum honest context.” Ruiz is not fully satisfied, but she accepts that change in public institutions is often gradual. “The important thing is that we are no longer pretending that one number tells the whole story,” she said. “A metric is a tool, not a truth.” The board will review the policy again next year, and the researchers have promised to publish their full data set so that others can check their conclusions. This commitment to transparency is seen by many as a positive step, ensuring that the debate remains evidence-based and open to public scrutiny.

questions.prompt: What does the participation rate measure, according to the passage?
options: The number of students who attend at least one session divided by the total number of students enrolled.
The average number of sessions attended by each student.
The number of students who attend ten or more sessions.
The total number of sessions offered by the clubs.
answers: The number of students who attend at least one session divided by the total number of students enrolled.
questions.explanation: 文章第一段明确说明参与率的计算方式：用至少参加一次课程的学生数除以全区注册学生总数。
questions.evidence: This figure is calculated by dividing the number of students who attend at least one session by the total number of students enrolled in the district.

questions.prompt: What did Elena Ruiz notice that seemed odd?
options: The participation rate was rising, but the number of students attending ten or more sessions had fallen.
The participation rate was falling, but more students were attending ten or more sessions.
The board had stopped reporting the participation rate.
Parents were complaining about the clubs.
answers: The participation rate was rising, but the number of students attending ten or more sessions had fallen.
questions.explanation: 第二段指出，Ruiz注意到参与率在上升，但参加十次或以上课程的学生人数却大幅下降。
questions.evidence: Although the participation rate was climbing, the number of students who attended ten or more sessions had fallen sharply.

questions.prompt: What was the average number of sessions per student after the three-year period?
questions.explanation: 第二段提到，人均参加课程数从6.2下降到3.8，因此三年后的平均数是3.8。
questions.evidence: They found that the average number of sessions attended per student had dropped from 6.2 to 3.8 over the same three-year period.

questions.prompt: Why did board member Priya Nair initially defend the participation rate?
options: Because it is simple to understand and cheap to collect.
Because it shows the depth of student engagement.
Because parents demanded a complex index.
answers: Because it is simple to understand and cheap to collect.
questions.explanation: 第三段中，Nair指出参与率简单易懂且收集成本低，这是她最初支持该指标的理由。
questions.evidence: A board member, Priya Nair, pointed out that the participation rate is simple to understand and cheap to collect.

questions.prompt: What did the parent evenings show?
options: Parents who saw only the single rate were more likely to say the clubs were doing well.
Parents who saw the dashboard were more confused than the others.
All parents preferred the single rate.
Parents who saw the dashboard remembered nothing.
answers: Parents who saw only the single rate were more likely to say the clubs were doing well.
questions.explanation: 第五段描述，只看到单一参与率的家长更可能说俱乐部“做得不错”，而看到仪表盘的家长更能同时看到优缺点。
questions.evidence: Those who saw only the single rate were more likely to say that the clubs were “doing well” and less likely to mention that attendance was shallow.

questions.prompt: What compromise is emerging for the annual report?
options: The participation rate will remain on the first page, accompanied by a short sentence about the average number of sessions per student.
The participation rate will be removed completely.
Only the dashboard will be published.
The board will stop publishing any numbers.
answers: The participation rate will remain on the first page, accompanied by a short sentence about the average number of sessions per student.
questions.explanation: 最后一段说明折中方案：参与率保留在年度报告第一页，但会附上一句关于人均课程数的简短说明。
questions.evidence: The participation rate will remain on the first page of the annual report, but it will be accompanied by a short sentence that states the average number of sessions per student.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best summarizes Dr. Haddad's view?
options: A misleading simple number is worse than a complex honest one.
Simplicity is always the most important value.
The participation rate should never be changed.
answers: A misleading simple number is worse than a complex honest one.
questions.explanation: 第三段中Haddad明确表示，一个误导性的简单数字比一个复杂的诚实数字更糟。
questions.evidence: Haddad agreed that simplicity has value, but he argued that a misleading simple number is worse than a complex honest one.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what will the researchers do next year?
options: Publish their full data set so that others can check their conclusions.
Replace the participation rate with a single new number.
answers: Publish their full data set so that others can check their conclusions.
questions.explanation: 文章结尾提到，研究人员承诺公布完整数据集，以便他人核查结论。
questions.evidence: the researchers have promised to publish their full data set so that others can check their conclusions.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: The participation rate was measuring breadth but not ______.
questions.explanation: 第二段结尾指出，参与率衡量的是广度而非深度，原文用词为depth。
questions.evidence: The participation rate, they concluded, was measuring breadth but not depth.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: Haddad calls the compromise a “minimum honest ______.”
questions.explanation: 最后一段中，Haddad将折中方案称为“minimum honest context”，即最低限度的诚实背景。
questions.evidence: Haddad calls this a “minimum honest context.”

grammar.title: 因果关系、条件和对比：段落间的逻辑与指代
grammar.explanation: 在英语写作中，表达因果、条件和对比时，除了使用从句（because, if, although），还常用名词化结构和连接副词来连接段落。例如：because of + 名词短语表示原因；if + 条件句表示条件；while/whereas 表示对比。同时，段落之间要用指代词（this, these, such, it）保持连贯，指代前文提到的概念。注意：this 单独使用时通常指代前一句或前一段的整体内容，而 this + 名词则明确指代某个名词。
grammar.example: Although the participation rate was climbing, the number of students who attended ten or more sessions had fallen sharply.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: ______ the heavy rain, the outdoor science fair was cancelled.
questions.explanation: “the heavy rain”是名词短语，表示原因，用Because of。Although和Despite表示让步，However是副词不能直接接名词。
questions.evidence: Because of the heavy rain, the outdoor science fair was cancelled.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: ______ students attend every session, they will receive a certificate.
questions.explanation: 句子表示条件“如果学生参加每次课程”，用If引导条件从句。
questions.evidence: If students attend every session, they will receive a certificate.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: The participation rate rose, ______ the average number of sessions fell.
questions.explanation: 前后两个分句形成对比：参与率上升，而平均课程数下降，用whereas表示对比。
questions.evidence: The participation rate rose, whereas the average number of sessions fell.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: The board ignored the teachers' concerns. ______, parents lost trust in the report.
questions.explanation: 前句是原因，后句是结果，用As a result表示“因此”。
questions.evidence: The board ignored the teachers' concerns. As a result, parents lost trust in the report.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: The researchers published their data. ______ allowed other scientists to check the results.
questions.explanation: This单独使用指代前一句的整体内容（公布数据这件事），作主语。
questions.evidence: The researchers published their data. This allowed other scientists to check the results.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: ______ the dashboard was more complex, parents understood the situation better.
questions.explanation: 前后是让步关系：尽管仪表盘更复杂，家长却理解得更好，用Although。
questions.evidence: Although the dashboard was more complex, parents understood the situation better.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: The board will adopt the new measure ______ the parents approve it.
questions.explanation: 表示条件“如果家长同意”，用if。unless表示“除非”，意思相反。
questions.evidence: The board will adopt the new measure if the parents approve it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: The report included three figures. ______ figures gave a fuller picture.
questions.explanation: 指代前句的复数名词figures，用These。
questions.evidence: The report included three figures. These figures gave a fuller picture.
